questions.q:
Which of the following are the example of double salt?

(A)& ${FeSO}_{4} \cdot \left({NH}_{4}\right)2{SO}_{4} \cdot 6{H}_{2}O$

(B)~${CuSO}_{4} \cdot 4{NH}_{3} \cdot {H}_{2}O$

(C)~${K}_{2}{SO}_{4} \cdot {Al}_{2}\left({SO}_{4}\right)3 \cdot 24{H}_{2}O$

(D)~$Fe ( CN{)}_{2} \cdot 4KCN$

Choose the correct answer.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
A& double salt& is a salt that contains two or more different cations or anions.

(A)& ${FeSO}_{4} + \left({NH}_{4}\right)2{SO}_{4} + 6{H}_{2}O \to {FeSO}_{4} \cdot \left({NH}_{4}\right)2{SO}_{4} \cdot 6{H}_{2}O$(Mohr's salt)

Mohr’s salt~called double salt which contains more than one simple salt. It undergoes complete dissociation in aqueous solutions.

(B)~${CuSO}_{4} \cdot 4{NH}_{3} \cdot {H}_{2}O$

Ammonia solution in water gives a blue precipitate when it combines with a solution of copper salt. The pale blue precipitate of copper hydroxide dissolves in excess of ammonium hydroxide forming tetraamine copper[II] sulphate, an azure blue (deep blue) soluble complex salt.

(C)~${K}_{2}{SO}_{4} \cdot {Al}_{2}\left({SO}_{4}\right)3 \cdot 24{H}_{2}O$~(Potash alum)

It is a double salt. Basically, it is comprised of two simple salts potassium sulphate and aluminium sulphate.~Potash alum will not be wet in its solid form because the water of crystallisation is not free.

(D)~$Fe ( CN{)}_{2} \cdot 4KCN$

It is complex salt. It does not dissociate completely into individual ions.

So, the correct answer is A and C only.

questions.q: Consider that& $d^{6}$~metal ion~  \left(M^{2 +}\right)$~forms a complex with aqua ligands, and the spin only magnetic moment of the complex is~$4 .90 BM$. The geometry and the crystal field stabilization energy of the complex is :$

questions.solution:
Since spin only magnetic moment is 4.90 BM so number of unpaired electrons must be 4.& There are two possibilities:

(1) If the complex is octahedral, then it has to be high spin complex with configuration ${t2g}^{2, 1, 1}{e}_g^{1, 1},$ in that case $CFSE = 4 \times \left(- 0 . 4{Δ}_{0}\right) + 2 \times 0 . 6{Δ}_{0} = - 0 . 4{Δ}_{0}$
(2) If the complex is tetrahedral then its electronic configuration will be $= {e}_{g}{t2g 2, 1}^{1, 1, 1}$ and $CFSE$ will $be = 3X\left(- 0 . 6{Δ}_{t}\right) + 3X\left(0 . 4{Δ}_{t}\right) = - 0 . 6\Deltat$

questions.q: $The oxidation states of iron atoms in compounds&  \left(A\right)$,~  \left(B\right)$~and~  \left(C\right)$, respectively, are~$x, y$~and~$z$. Then sum of~$x, y$~and~$z$~is ...........~$\mathop{{Na}_{4}\left[Fe\left(CN\right)5\left(NOS\right)\right]}_{A}\mathop{{Na}_{4}\left[{FeO}_{4}\right]}_{B}\mathop{{Fe}_{2}\left(CO\right)9}_{C}$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Oxidation state of& $Fe$~in~${Na}_{4} \left[Fe \left(CN\right)5 \left(NOS\right)\right]$:

Charge of~$CN$~=$- 1$

Charge of~$NOS = - 1$

Suppose oxidation state of~$Fe = x$

$4 + x - 5 - 1 = 0 ⇒ x = + 2$

Oxidation state of~$Fein{Na}_{4} \left[{FeO}_{4}\right]:

$4 + x - 8 = 0 ⇒ x = + 4$

Oxidation state of~$Fein \left[{Fe}_{2} \left(CO\right)9\right]$~$= 0$~because carbonyl is neutral ligand.

The oxidation states of iron in these compounds will be

$A = + 2B = + 4C = 0$

The sum of oxidation states will be $= 6$.

$
